# featbit_member_direct_policies (Resource)

Authoritatively manages one existing FeatBit Member's complete direct Policy set through the documented public API. It never manages inherited Group Policies, Group bindings, or the Member lifecycle.

## Authoritative ownership

`policy_ids` is the complete intended direct Policy set, not a list of
additions. Apply removes every current direct Policy that is not configured.
An empty set removes all direct Policies, and destroying this Terraform
resource also clears the Member's current direct set before dropping state.

Group membership and inherited Group Policies are never read as owned state
and are never changed. The Member itself must already exist and remains
external to Terraform lifecycle management.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "member_email" {
  description = "Organization-scoped full email of the existing Member whose direct Policies will be managed."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "direct_policy_keys" {
  description = "Complete intended set of organization-scoped exact direct Policy keys for the Member."
  type        = set(string)
}

data "featbit_member" "target" {
  email = var.member_email
}

data "featbit_policy" "direct" {
  for_each = var.direct_policy_keys

  key = each.value
}

resource "featbit_member_direct_policies" "example" {
  member_id = data.featbit_member.target.id
  policy_ids = toset([
    for policy in data.featbit_policy.direct : policy.id
  ])
}
```

The example intentionally has no default for `direct_policy_keys`: supply the
complete intended set explicitly. Before the first apply, account for every
current direct Policy and review the plan. Omitting a Policy authorizes its
removal. Member identifiers are Sensitive, and Terraform state and plans must
be handled as confidential.

## Lifecycle

- `policy_ids` can contain custom or built-in Policy UUIDs and updates in
  place as one authoritative set.
- `member_id` changes require replacement.
- Additions are confirmed before removals begin. Each pair mutation executes
  once, with confirmed intermediate state retained after partial failure.
- Destroy clears direct Policies only; it never removes Group bindings,
  inherited Policies, or the Member.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `member_id` (String, Sensitive) Exact existing Member UUID. Changing it replaces this authoritative direct-Policy set.
- `policy_ids` (Set of String) Complete unordered set of direct custom or built-in Policy UUIDs. An empty set removes every direct Policy without changing inherited Policies.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String, Sensitive) Canonical Member UUID, equal to `member_id`.

## Import

Import the direct-Policy set for one existing Member:

```shell
terraform import featbit_member_direct_policies.example '<member_uuid>'
```

The identifier is the Member UUID in 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form. Import sets
that identity, and refresh reads the current direct set into state; the next
plan still compares it with the complete `policy_ids` configured in HCL.
Review that plan before applying.
